obn_stillman.text: Barley, water and yeast. That's the lot. We malt it, mash it, ferment it, then double distil it in copper stills that are small enough to look like they belong in a cottage.
The town grew up around this place in 1794. We've outlasted the town council, three bypasses and all the ferries that said they'd never come back.

obn_cooper.text: A cooper makes the casks. Barrels that held sherry or bourbon, mostly. The wood gives the whisky its colour, and a good deal of the flavour.
About two per cent of the whisky evaporates out of every cask every year. That's called the angel's share. The angels, in Scotland, are heavy drinkers.
